think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 48-year-old man with a 25-year history of relapsing brainstem neurological deficits and biopsy-proven mediastinal non-caseating epithelioid granulomas (treated as neurosarcoidosis with steroids and methotrexate) developed a chest wall mass and pleural effusion. The key tension is distinguishing an aggressive extrapulmonary flare of sarcoidosis from opportunistic reactivation of mycobacterial infection unmasked by cumulative immunosuppression.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The breakpoint occurs when the patient presents with the new chest wall mass and pleural effusion while on maintenance immunosuppression, immediately prior to thoracentesis, empyema drainage, and molecular microbiological testing.
3. Differential Distinctions: Relapsing demyelination / multiple sclerosis was ruled out by negative CSF oligoclonal bands and non-neural mediastinal granulomas; sarcoidosis flare was considered given prior mediastinal non-caseating granulomas, but pleural fluid analysis yielded rifampin-sensitive Mycobacterium tuberculosis by GeneXpert.
case_prompt: A 48-year-old man with a 25-year history of relapsing and remitting brainstem neurologic deficits and mediastinal lymphadenopathy—previously treated with corticosteroids and maintenance methotrexate for histologically-proven non-caseating epithelioid granulomas—presented after developing a new mass on the anterior chest wall accompanied by an ipsilateral pleural effusion. Prior to the onset of the chest wall mass, his neurological symptoms had stabilized on immunosuppressive therapy, but he now noted localized thoracic discomfort and progressive pleural fluid accumulation. Vital signs and initial bedside evaluation confirmed the presence of a palpable chest wall mass and unilateral dullness to percussion over the hemithorax.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Thoracoscopic lymph node biopsy had demonstrated non-caseating epithelioid granulomas consistent with sarcoidosis with negative initial mycobacterial testing; however, following immunosuppressive therapy with corticosteroids and methotrexate, the emergence of a chest wall mass and empyema was proven to be active mycobacterial disease rather than sarcoid progression.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: However, during this course, chest computed tomography (CT) revealed multiple enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes, and thoracoscopic lymph node biopsy showed many epithelioid granulomas (Figures 1K,L). The GeneXpert assay, AFB culture, and Mycobacterium tuberculosis polymerase chain reaction (MTB PCR) test on the lymph node were all negative for MTB. The biopsy findings were consistent with sarcoidosis, so methotrexate was added.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Relapsing inflammatory brainstem demyelination / Multiple sclerosis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to episodic brainstem neurological deficits with pontine enhancement responsive to high-dose corticosteroids; however, CSF oligoclonal bands were negative, serum autoantibodies and inflammatory markers were normal, and the patient subsequently manifested non-neural thoracic granulomatous lesions and empyema.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: CSF analysis showed mild pleocytosis (8 cells/muL) with a lymphocyte predominance. Serum and CSF oligoclonal bands were negative. Acid-fast bacteria (AFB) stains and cultures were negative. He was diagnosed with relapsing inflammatory demyelination of the brain stem.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: In 2020, while maintained on methotrexate and corticosteroids, the patient developed a new chest wall mass and pleural effusion; GeneXpert molecular testing of the empyema fluid was positive for rifampin-sensitive Mycobacterium tuberculosis, establishing active pulmonary and pleural disease.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: In 2020, the patient developed a pleural effusion and a mass on the chest wall. The GeneXpert testing of empyema was positive for MTB, which is sensitive to rifampin. He was diagnosed with pulmonary TB.

editor_comments: Case illustrates diagnostic dilemma between neurosarcoidosis and pulmonary tuberculosis where chronic immunosuppression unmasked active tuberculous empyema and chest wall cold abscess.
